*Analysis and figures for a technical paper documenting the design and application of whorlmap, the uncertainty aware heatmap.*

Whorlmap is a compact heatmap design for high-dimensional comparisons where each cell encodes a full bootstrapped effect size distribution as a tiny spiral, rather than collapsing uncertainty into a single color. It lets readers scan many treatment–outcome contrasts at once while still seeing direction, magnitude, and uncertainty inside each cell. (Read more on [effect size estimation (and the replication crisis)](https://xusangyu.com/blog/01_dabest.html)? and [why bootstrap](https://acclab.github.io/DABEST-python/blog/posts/bootstraps/bootstraps.html)?) 

![**Figure 1. The whorlmap encodes bootstrap distributions in a compact heatmap.** **(Ai–Aiii)** A synthetic two-group comparison (20 observations per group) illustrates the encoding: a Gardner–Altman estimation plot shows the raw observations and bootstrap mean difference with its 95% confidence interval (CI; Ai); the bootstrap distribution is represented as a 7 × 7-pixel whorl cell (Aii) and a histogram segmented by the same quantile boundaries (Aiii). The outer 2.5% of each tail is omitted from the whorl cell. Pixel position follows an outside-in spiral, and colour encodes effect size. **(Bi–Bv)** Example distributions illustrate large positive and negative effects with narrow intervals, a near-zero effect, broad uncertainty, and multimodality, respectively. **(Ci–Cii)** Sex differences in expression of 20 neuroactive and glial genes across 13 brain regions from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project, version 8, shown as a whorlmap with selected bootstrap distributions (Ci) and a scalar heatmap of mean differences (Cii). Effects are female minus male mean expression on the log₂(TPM + 1) scale (TPM, transcripts per million), estimated with 5,000 bootstrap resamples per comparison. Highlighted pairs (a1/a2 and b1/b2) show how similar mean differences can conceal differences in distribution width and shape. Warm colours indicate positive effects; cool colours indicate negative effects.](nbs/images/figure1_assembly.png){width=500px fig-align="center" fig-alt="Ai shows two groups of observations with an effect estimate. Aii and Aiii link a spiral pixel grid to a coloured histogram. Bi through Bv show five contrasting pixel patterns above their distributions. Ci has brain regions in rows and genes in columns, with four outlined cells linked to distributions at right. Cii replaces the pixel patterns with uniform colours and numerical means, obscuring differences in uncertainty."}

## Notebooks

| Notebook | Description |
|---|---|
| [Figure 1](nbs/figure1.ipynb) | GTEx sex-difference analysis across 13 brain regions × 20 genes — the main paper figure |
| [Data Pipeline](nbs/helpers/survey.ipynb) | GTEx v8 download, stream-parse, and metadata generation |
| [Cache Builder](nbs/helpers/make_cache.ipynb) | Slice full GTEx to the 20 display genes → committed 514 KB cache |

## Reproduce Figure 1

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sangyu/whorlmap-paper
cd whorlmap-paper/nbs
pip install dabest pandas numpy matplotlib seaborn scipy Pillow svgutils lxml nbconvert ipykernel
jupyter notebook figure1.ipynb
```

`figure1.ipynb` loads the committed expression cache and runs `dabest.combine()` live.
Bootstraps, whorlmap, and all panels are generated fresh. Runtime ~10–15 min.

## Data

Gene expression data are from GTEx v8:

> GTEx Consortium. The GTEx Consortium atlas of genetic regulatory effects across human tissues. *Science* 369, 1318–1330 (2020). <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaz1776>
